Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS: The statement’s read on solid activity and low, stable unemployment is tempered by still-elevated inflation and greater uncertainty. Policy is held steady at 4.25–4.5 percent, with implementation settings (IORB 4.4 percent, ON RRP 4.25 percent, standing repo 4.5 percent) consistent with a floor system and gradual balance-sheet runoff via relatively small caps.

April SLOOS signals tighter credit supply and softer demand, especially outside the largest banks: foreign banks and other banks tightened C&I terms while large banks left C&I standards broadly unchanged; banks tightened CRE lending standards, and CRE loan demand weakened (reported by foreign and large banks). Banks cited the economic outlook, supervisory actions, risk tolerance, and other factors, alongside weaker customer financing needs and investment. These findings point to headwinds for credit availability and activity—particularly in CRE and some business segments—even as bank core resilience remains adequate.

Net: current conditions are slightly positive, but tighter credit from SLOOS and financial-stability vulnerabilities shift the overall tone from near-neutral to slightly cautious/negative. sentiment score = -0.05
